name: Pendulum swings
goal: Reduce pain and allow gentle early movement
conditions: Frozen shoulder, post-surgery, rotator cuff pain
position: Standing, lean forward with one hand on a table, affected arm hanging
how: Let the arm hang loose. Gently sway the body so the arm swings forward and back, side to side, then in small circles.
dose: 2 min each direction, 2 to 3 times daily
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp or you feel dizzy

name: Table slides
goal: Restore forward lifting of the arm
conditions: Stiff shoulder, after fracture or surgery
position: Sitting at a table, hand on a towel
how: Slide the hand forward, leaning the body forward, then return.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Wall slides
position: Standing facing a wall, forearms on the wall
how: Slide the forearms up the wall while stepping gently closer.
progression: Add a light band around the wrists
precautions: Stop if there is a sharp pinch at the top

name: Cross-body stretch
goal: Keep the back of the shoulder flexible
position: Standing or sitting
how: Bring the arm across the chest and hold it with the other hand just above the elbow.
precautions: Keep the stretch mild, under 4 of 10

name: Doorway chest stretch
goal: Ease tight chest muscles and rounded posture
position: Standing in a doorway, forearms on the frame
how: Step through gently until you feel a stretch across the chest.
progression: Raise or lower the arm height
precautions: Stop if there is tingling in the arm

name: Band external rotation
position: Standing, elbow bent at the side with a rolled towel under it
how: Hold a band and turn the forearm outward, then slowly return.
dose: 3 x 12, daily or every other day
progression: Thicker band, then arm at 90 degrees
precautions: Pain above 4 of 10 means reduce the band or stop

name: Band internal rotation
goal: Strengthen the muscles that turn the arm inward
conditions: Rotator cuff problems, post-surgery later phase
position: Standing, elbow at the side, band anchored at the door
how: Pull the forearm inward across the belly, then slowly return.
dose: 3 x 12, daily or every other day
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Scapular squeeze
goal: Improve shoulder blade control and posture
conditions: Neck and shoulder pain, rounded shoulders
position: Sitting or standing tall
how: Draw the shoulder blades back and down as if tucking them into back pockets. Hold, then relax.
dose: 2 x 10, hold 5 s, several times a day
precautions: Do not shrug the shoulders up

name: Prone T raise
goal: Strengthen the muscles between and below the shoulder blades
position: Lying face down, arms out to the side
how: Lift the arms to shoulder height with thumbs up, hold 2 s, lower slowly.
precautions: Stop if the neck or shoulder pinches

name: Wall push-up plus
position: Standing facing a wall, arms straight on the wall
how: Push the wall away and round the upper back slightly at the end. Return slowly.
progression: Move to a table, then the floor
precautions: Stop if the shoulder feels unstable

name: Isometric shoulder abduction on a wall
position: Standing sideways, back of the hand against a wall, elbow slightly bent
how: Press the arm gently into the wall without moving. Hold.
precautions: Effort should feel mild to moderate, pain under 4 of 10

name: Active shoulder movement screen
goal: Record range of movement and compare both sides
position: Standing, facing the camera, then side-on
how: Raise the arm forward and out to the side as high as possible, both sides. Reach hand behind head and behind back. Record where pain starts.
dose: One slow attempt each movement, both sides
precautions: Do not push into sharp pain

name: Painful arc check
goal: Find the range where the shoulder hurts
position: Standing facing the camera
how: Raise the arm out to the side slowly to overhead and lower slowly. Say when pain starts and stops.
precautions: Stop if pain is severe

name: Reach behind head and back (Apley scratch)
goal: Check combined reach used in dressing and grooming
position: Standing
how: Reach one hand over the shoulder and the other up the back, then swap sides. Note how close the hands get.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Eccentric wrist extension
goal: Load the tendon at the outer elbow
position: Forearm on a table, palm down, wrist off the edge, light weight in hand
how: Use the other hand to lift the wrist up, then slowly lower it with the affected hand over 3 to 4 seconds.
precautions: Pain up to 4 of 10 is acceptable if it settles within a day

name: Eccentric wrist flexion
goal: Load the tendon at the inner elbow
position: Forearm on a table, palm up, wrist off the edge, light weight
how: Use the other hand to lift the wrist up, then slowly lower it over 3 to 4 seconds.
precautions: Stop if pain stays high the next day

name: Elbow bend and straighten
position: Sitting, arm supported on a table
how: Bend the elbow as far as comfortable, then straighten fully. Hold briefly at both ends.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp, or swelling increases

name: Forearm turn (pronation and supination)
position: Sitting, elbow bent to 90 degrees, tucked at the side
how: Turn the palm up, then down, slowly through full range.
progression: Hold a light hammer or bottle
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Median nerve glide
goal: Ease nerve tension in the arm and hand
position: Sitting, arm out to the side
how: Move the wrist and head gently in opposite directions in a flowing motion. Do not hold a stretch.
precautions: Stop if tingling or pain increases

name: Wrist stretches
conditions: Wrist stiffness, desk and phone use
position: Sitting, arm out in front
how: With the other hand, gently bend the wrist up and then down. Hold each.
precautions: Stop if tingling occurs

name: Tendon glides
position: Sitting, hand in front
how: Move the fingers through straight, hook, full fist, table top and straight fist, one position at a time.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Squeeze a soft ball
position: Sitting, forearm on a table
how: Squeeze a ball or rolled towel firmly for 5 seconds, then relax.
precautions: Stop if joints become painful

name: Thumb to each fingertip
position: Sitting, hand in front
how: Touch the thumb to each fingertip in turn, making a round O shape.
progression: Do it faster or with eyes closed
precautions: Stop if painful

name: Finger spread with a band
position: Sitting, hand in front, band around the fingers
how: Spread the fingers against the band, hold 3 seconds, relax.
precautions: Stop if joints hurt

name: Coin pick-up timing
position: Sitting at a table, 10 coins spread out and a cup
how: Pick up the coins one at a time and drop them in the cup. Time the task. Do both hands.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Static quadriceps contraction
goal: Wake up the thigh muscle early
conditions: After knee surgery or injury, knee arthritis
position: Lying or sitting with the leg straight, small towel under the knee
how: Tighten the front of the thigh and press the knee down into the towel. Hold 5 s.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Straight leg raise
goal: Strengthen the thigh without bending the knee
position: Lying on the back, other knee bent
how: Tighten the thigh, lift the straight leg to the height of the other knee, lower slowly.
precautions: Do not let the knee bend or the back arch

name: Heel slides
position: Lying on the back
how: Slide the heel toward the buttock as far as comfortable, hold 5 s, slide back.
progression: Use a strap for more bend
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp, or the knee swells more

name: Seated knee extension
position: Sitting on a chair
how: Straighten the knee, hold 3 s, lower slowly.
precautions: Pain behind the kneecap above 4 of 10 means reduce the range

name: Terminal knee extension with a band
goal: Strengthen the last part of knee straightening
conditions: After knee ligament injury, patellofemoral pain
position: Standing, band behind the knee anchored in front
how: Start with the knee slightly bent and straighten it fully against the band.
precautions: Stop if the knee gives way

name: Mini squat
goal: Build leg strength in a safe range
position: Standing, holding a counter
how: Bend the knees to about 45 degrees, keep the knees over the toes, stand up.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp, or knees fall inward

name: Sit-to-stand from a chair
conditions: Older adults, knee arthritis, after hospital stay
position: Sitting on a firm chair, arms crossed
how: Stand up fully, then sit down slowly.
progression: Lower the chair or hold a weight
precautions: Stop if dizzy or short of breath

name: Step-ups
position: Standing in front of a low step
how: Step up, bring the other foot up, step down slowly.
dose: 3 x 10 each leg, every other day
precautions: Keep the knee in line with the second toe

name: Wall squat hold
goal: Reduce pain from the kneecap tendon
position: Back against a wall, feet forward
how: Slide down to a comfortable angle and hold.
precautions: Pain up to 4 of 10 is acceptable if settling

name: Standing hamstring curl
goal: Strengthen the back of the thigh
position: Standing, holding a counter
how: Bend the heel toward the buttock, hold 2 s, lower slowly.
precautions: Stop if sharp pain at the back of the thigh

name: Seated hamstring stretch
goal: Keep the back of the thigh flexible
conditions: Tight hamstrings, back and knee pain
position: Sitting at the edge of a chair, one leg straight with heel on the floor
how: Lean forward from the hips with a straight back until you feel a stretch.
precautions: Do not round the back

name: Active knee extension lag check
goal: Check if the thigh can fully straighten the knee
position: Sitting, lower leg hanging
how: Straighten the knee fully without help. Note how many degrees short it stays.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Bodyweight squat screen
goal: Observe movement quality and knee control
position: Standing facing the camera, then side-on
how: Squat down as far as comfortable and stand. Check if knees fall in, heels lift or weight shifts.
precautions: Stop if sharp pain

name: 30-second chair stand test
goal: Measure lower limb strength and fall risk
conditions: Older adults, knee or hip problems
position: Sitting on a chair about 43 cm high, arms crossed
how: Stand up and sit down as many times as possible in 30 seconds. Count full stands.
precautions: Do not do if dizzy or unsteady without help nearby

name: Timed up and go
position: Sitting on a chair, a mark 3 metres away
how: Stand, walk to the mark, turn, walk back, sit. Time it at a safe, usual pace.
precautions: Do with another person nearby

name: Ankle pumps
goal: Reduce swelling and keep the ankle moving
conditions: After sprain, fracture, surgery, long sitting or bed rest
position: Lying or sitting, leg raised
how: Point the toes away, then pull them toward you, steadily.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Ankle alphabet
goal: Restore ankle movement in all directions
position: Sitting, foot off the floor
how: Draw each letter of the alphabet with the big toe.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Four-way ankle band exercises
position: Sitting, band around the forefoot
how: Push the foot down, pull it up, turn it in and out against the band.
precautions: Stop if sharp pain or swelling

name: Calf stretch on a wall
position: Standing facing a wall, one leg back with the heel down
how: Lean toward the wall keeping the back knee straight and the heel down.
progression: Bend the back knee to stretch the lower calf
precautions: Stop if pain in the heel is sharp

name: Heel raises
conditions: Achilles tendinopathy, ankle sprain, older adults
position: Standing, holding a counter
how: Rise onto the toes, hold 2 s, lower slowly.
precautions: Stop if the Achilles pain is sharp

name: Eccentric heel drop
position: Standing on a step, heels hanging off the edge
how: Rise on both feet, shift to the sore leg and lower the heel slowly over 3 to 4 seconds.
precautions: Pain up to 4 of 10 acceptable if it settles by next morning

name: Towel scrunches
position: Sitting with a towel under the foot
how: Scrunch the towel toward you using the toes.
progression: Place a light weight on the towel
precautions: Stop if foot cramps

name: Short foot exercise
position: Sitting or standing, foot flat
how: Draw the ball of the foot toward the heel to lift the arch without curling the toes. Hold 5 s.
progression: Do it standing, then on one leg
precautions: Stop if the foot cramps

name: Plantar fascia stretch
position: Sitting, ankle crossed over the other knee
how: Pull the toes back toward the shin until you feel a stretch under the arch.
dose: 3 x 30 s, before standing in the morning
precautions: Stop if the heel pain is sharp

name: Single-leg balance
position: Standing next to a counter
how: Stand on one leg. Eyes open, then closed.
precautions: Keep a counter within reach

name: Single-leg stance test
conditions: Ankle instability, older adults, neurological conditions
position: Standing next to a counter
how: Stand on one leg with hands on the hips. Time until the foot touches down. Repeat eyes closed if safe.
precautions: Do with another person nearby

name: Knee-to-wall lunge test
position: Standing facing a wall, foot on a line
how: Lunge so the knee touches the wall with the heel down. Move the foot back until the heel just lifts. Measure the distance.
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp

name: Heel walk and toe walk screen
goal: Check ankle strength and nerve function
conditions: Foot drop, nerve or Achilles problems
position: Standing, a 5 metre path
how: Walk on the heels, then on the toes. Note which side is weak.
precautions: Do with a counter or person nearby

name: Glute bridge
goal: Strengthen the buttock and back of the thigh
conditions: Hip and back pain, post-surgery later phase
position: Lying on the back, knees bent
how: Tighten the buttocks and lift the hips until the body is straight from shoulders to knees. Hold 3 s.
precautions: Stop if the back or hamstring cramps

name: Clamshell
goal: Strengthen the side of the hip
conditions: Gluteal tendinopathy, hip and knee pain
position: Lying on the side, knees bent, heels together
how: Lift the top knee without rolling the pelvis back. Lower slowly.
precautions: Stop if the hip pain is sharp

name: Side-lying hip abduction
position: Lying on the side, bottom leg bent
how: Lift the top leg straight up and slightly back, lower slowly.
precautions: Do not roll the hips backward

name: Standing hip abduction with a band
goal: Strengthen hips for walking and balance
position: Standing, holding a counter, band around the ankles
how: Lift one leg out to the side keeping the body upright.
precautions: Do not lean the body sideways

name: Hip flexor stretch
conditions: Sitting desk workers, low back and hip pain
position: Kneeling on one knee, other foot forward, on a cushion
how: Tighten the buttock of the kneeling side and shift forward gently until you feel a stretch at the front of the hip.
precautions: Do not arch the lower back

name: Figure-4 stretch
position: Lying on the back, ankle on the opposite knee
how: Pull the lower thigh toward the chest until you feel a stretch in the buttock.
precautions: Stop if you feel pinching in the front of the hip

name: Hip hinge
goal: Learn to bend from the hips and protect the back
position: Standing, a stick along the back
how: Push the hips back, keeping the back straight, then return by squeezing the buttocks.
precautions: Keep the stick touching head, mid back and tailbone

name: Bridge march
position: In a bridge position
how: Lift one foot a few centimetres without the hips dropping, then swap.
precautions: Stop if the back hurts

name: Ball squeeze (adductor)
position: Lying on the back, knees bent, soft ball between knees
how: Squeeze the ball, hold 5 s, relax.
precautions: Stop if groin pain is sharp

name: Hip movement screen
position: Sitting, then lying
how: Lift the knee toward the chest, then turn the foot in and out with the knee bent. Compare both sides and note pain.
precautions: Stop if pinching or sharp pain

name: Single-leg stance for pelvic drop (Trendelenburg)
conditions: Hip pain, limp, after hip surgery
position: Standing facing the camera from behind
how: Lift one foot and hold 30 seconds. The clinician checks if the pelvis drops on the lifted side.
precautions: Do next to a counter

name: Hip flexor length check
position: Lying near the edge of a bed, one knee held to the chest
how: Let the other leg hang off the edge and relax. The clinician observes thigh and knee position.
precautions: Stop if pinching in the hip

name: Figure-4 position check
conditions: Hip arthritis, groin or buttock pain
position: Lying on the back
how: Place one ankle on the other knee and let the knee fall outward. Note height and where the pain is felt.
precautions: Stop if sharp pain

name: Chin tuck
goal: Reduce neck strain and forward head posture
position: Sitting or standing tall
how: Gently draw the chin straight back as if making a double chin. Hold 5 s.
progression: Do lying down, then add a head lift
precautions: Stop if dizzy or arm symptoms worsen

name: Neck range of movement
position: Sitting tall
how: Turn the head to each side, tilt the ear toward each shoulder, then look down and up gently.
precautions: Stop if dizzy, or if arm tingling worsens

name: Upper trapezius stretch
goal: Ease tension at the top of the shoulder
position: Sitting tall, hand under the seat
how: Tilt the head away from the held side until you feel a stretch.
precautions: Do not force the neck

name: Levator scapulae stretch
goal: Ease tension at the back of the neck
position: Sitting tall
how: Turn the nose toward the armpit and gently look down, with a light hand pull.
precautions: Do not force the neck

name: Deep neck flexor lift
goal: Strengthen the deep muscles at the front of the neck
position: Lying on the back with the knees bent
how: Nod the chin gently, then lift the head a finger width off the pillow. Hold 5 to 10 s.
precautions: Stop if neck strain is sharp

name: Neck rotation measure
goal: Measure how far the neck turns
position: Sitting tall facing the camera
how: Turn the head to each side as far as comfortable. Use a phone angle app or the camera view to compare both sides.
precautions: Stop if dizzy or tingling

name: Deep neck flexor endurance
position: Lying on the back with the knees bent
how: Nod the chin and lift the head slightly. Time how long it can be held.
precautions: Stop if neck strain is sharp

name: Thoracic extension over a chair
position: Sitting on a chair with the upper back against the top of the chair back, hands behind the head
how: Lean back over the chair back and look up gently. Hold briefly.
precautions: Support the head, do not force

name: Open book
conditions: Stiff upper back, rib or shoulder tightness
position: Lying on the side, knees bent, arms in front
how: Lift the top arm up and across to open the chest and follow it with your eyes. Return.
precautions: Stop if sharp pain

name: Wall angels
goal: Improve upper back and shoulder posture
position: Standing with back and head against a wall
how: Slide the arms up and down like making a snow angel, keeping contact with the wall.
progression: Move feet closer to the wall
precautions: Stop if pinching in the shoulders

name: Diaphragmatic breathing
goal: Relax the chest and back and improve breathing
conditions: Back pain, stress, chronic lung problems
position: Lying with knees bent, one hand on the belly
how: Breathe in through the nose so the belly rises, breathe out slowly. Keep the chest still.
precautions: Stop if dizzy

name: Pelvic tilt
goal: Gentle movement and awareness of the lower back
conditions: Acute and chronic low back pain
position: Lying on the back, knees bent
how: Flatten the back to the floor by tightening the belly, then relax.
precautions: Stop if leg pain increases

name: Knee-to-chest stretch
position: Lying on the back
how: Hug one knee, then both, toward the chest. Hold.
precautions: Avoid if leg pain increases

name: Cat and camel
position: On hands and knees
how: Arch the back up, then let it sag gently, moving slowly.
precautions: Stop if wrist or knee pain

name: Bird dog
position: On hands and knees
how: Reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back, hold 5 s, keeping the back still. Swap.
precautions: Stop if the back sags or pain increases

name: Dead bug
position: Lying on the back, hips and knees bent to 90 degrees
how: Lower the opposite arm and leg slowly toward the floor while keeping the back flat. Return.
precautions: Stop if the back arches or hurts

name: Prone lying and prone press-up
goal: Reduce leg and back pain that eases with extension
conditions: Disc related low back pain with a directional preference
position: Lying face down, then on the elbows, then hands
how: Rest on the stomach, then slowly press up on the elbows, then straight arms, keeping the hips down.
precautions: Stop if pain spreads further down the leg

name: Knee rolls (lumbar rotation)
goal: Ease stiffness in the lower back
position: Lying on the back, knees bent
how: Let both knees fall to one side, then the other, slowly.
precautions: Stop if pain increases

name: Child's pose
position: On hands and knees
how: Sit back onto the heels with the arms stretched forward. Hold.
progression: Walk the hands to each side
precautions: Avoid if knee pain or in late pregnancy without advice

name: Side plank on the knees
goal: Strengthen the sides of the trunk
position: Lying on the side, knees bent, on the elbow
how: Lift the hips so the body is straight from shoulders to knees. Hold.
precautions: Stop if the shoulder or back hurts

name: Curl-up
goal: Strengthen the belly muscles with low spine load
position: Lying on the back, one knee bent, hands under the lower back
how: Lift the head and shoulders just off the floor. Hold 5 to 7 s.
precautions: Avoid with acute disc pain

name: Sciatic nerve glide
position: Sitting on a chair
how: Slump gently, straighten the knee while looking up, then bend the knee while looking down.
precautions: Stop if leg symptoms worsen

name: Standing back extension
goal: Reduce pain in a stooped posture
conditions: Low back pain with extension preference
position: Standing, hands on the lower back
how: Lean back gently over the hands. Return.
precautions: Stop if leg symptoms increase

name: Graded walking
conditions: Chronic low back pain, general fitness
position: Outdoors or indoors
how: Walk at an easy pace. Add 1 to 2 minutes each day when the pain is acceptable.
precautions: Pain up to 4 of 10 is acceptable if it settles within a day

name: Lumbar movement screen
goal: Check direction of pain and movement
position: Standing, side-on to the camera
how: Bend forward, lean back and slide the hand down each side. Note range and where pain appears.
precautions: Stop if leg pain or numbness appears

name: Active straight leg raise
goal: Check leg and nerve mobility and pain
position: Lying on the back
how: Raise one straight leg as far as comfortable. Note the angle and where pain or pulling is felt.
precautions: Stop if sharp leg pain

name: Back extensor endurance test (Sorensen)
conditions: Chronic low back pain, return to sport
position: Lying face down, upper body off the edge of a bed supported by a helper
how: Hold the upper body level as long as possible. Time it.
precautions: Not for acute pain, osteoporosis or severe back pain

name: Eyebrow raise
conditions: Bell's palsy, facial weakness after stroke
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Lift both eyebrows slowly. Use the fingers on the healthy side to guide symmetry.
precautions: Stop if the face becomes tired or twitching increases

name: Gentle eye closure
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Close both eyes gently without squeezing hard, then open.
precautions: Protect the eye with drops if it does not close fully

name: Nose wrinkle
goal: Activate the muscles around the nose
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Wrinkle the nose as if smelling something unpleasant, then relax.
precautions: Stop if the face becomes tired

name: Closed-lip smile
goal: Restore smiling and mouth corner movement
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Smile with lips closed, aiming for equal lift on both sides.
progression: Hold 3 s, then smile with teeth
precautions: Do not over-pull the healthy side

name: Cheek puff
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Fill the cheeks with air and hold the lips tight. Move the air from side to side.
precautions: Stop if air leaks and the face tires

name: Lip pucker and release
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Pucker the lips as if giving a kiss, hold 3 s, then relax into a smile.
precautions: Stop if the face becomes tired

name: Mirror-guided movement sequence
goal: Keep the face symmetrical while recovering
conditions: Bell's palsy recovery, facial weakness after stroke
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Do each movement slowly and in order: brows, eyes, nose, smile, pucker. Stop any movement that pulls the face to one side.
precautions: Stop if the face twitches or tightens

name: Warm cloth and gentle facial massage
position: Sitting
how: Apply a warm cloth, then use gentle upward circles on the cheek and forehead.
precautions: Avoid if skin is irritated or numb to heat

name: Controlled jaw opening (6 by 6)
position: Sitting, tongue resting on the roof of the mouth
how: Open the mouth slowly with the tongue up, then close. Keep the jaw moving straight.
precautions: Stop if the jaw clicks painfully or locks

name: Resting jaw position
position: Anywhere
how: Keep the lips together, teeth apart and the tongue resting on the roof of the mouth. Check this a few times each hour.
precautions: Stop if the jaw feels tense

name: Side-to-side jaw glide
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Move the lower jaw slowly to the left, back to centre, then to the right.
progression: A small piece of rubber between the teeth for more range, if advised
precautions: Stop if pain is sharp or the jaw locks

name: Jaw muscle self-massage
position: Sitting
how: Use the finger pads to gently massage the muscle at the cheek and temple in small circles.
precautions: Stop if the pain increases

name: Three-finger jaw opening test
goal: Measure how far the jaw opens
position: Sitting in front of a mirror
how: Open the mouth as wide as comfortable and check if three stacked fingers fit between the teeth. Note pain and any jaw shift.
precautions: Stop if the jaw locks

name: Facial symmetry movement screen
goal: Record facial movement on each side
position: Sitting facing the camera
how: Raise the brows, close the eyes, smile and pucker. Record how well each side moves and compare with the last visit.
precautions: Stop if the eye cannot close and dries
